problemStatement: WR-009 and WR-011 provide complete rendered Telegram Markdown and semantic chunks, but no delivery adapter boundary exists for a later Telegram transport. A direct provider implementation here would mix transport concerns, secrets, and publication lifecycle behavior into the interface. User-facing product motivation was not separately provided.

riskAssessment.reason: The adapter must forward complete source chunks in order, propagate transport failures without inventing receipts or retries, and remain free of network, secret, and domain dependencies.
riskAssessment.reviewNotes: WR-011 exposes complete chunks and boundary labels. The transport is injected as a local trait so tests can prove ordering and error propagation without external I/O.

reasons: Medium-risk interface adapter with explicit local verification and no external publication.

acceptance: A public provider-agnostic TelegramTransport trait accepts a destination and complete Markdown payload without prescribing an HTTP client, credentials, or provider SDK; its rustdoc explains the boundary.
TelegramPublisherAdapter consumes WR-011 SemanticMessageSplit chunks, forwards each complete chunk once in source order, and never truncates, re-renders, merges, or recalculates content.
Transport failures return a typed adapter error containing the failing chunk index and semantic boundary, stop subsequent sends, and do not implement retry, receipt, or message-ID behavior.
Blank destination and empty split are rejected locally before transport invocation; no real network or external side effect is performed by tests or production code.
Module-local, same-stem companion, and public integration tests cover forwarding, exact content/order, failure propagation, empty input, and provider/lifecycle isolation.

The WR-010 spec and plan name the adapter files and tests; the reference-impact record covers the infrastructure registration and new adapter; the Summary records `make check`, focused tests, AI Cockpit gates, strict Finish/Archive, the local commit, and the authorized publish/merge/close handoff.
guidelines: New public APIs must be documented.
Do not import internal modules from other features.
Keep the adapter provider-agnostic and do not add secrets or machine-specific paths.

intent.problem: WR-009 and WR-011 produce complete, already-rendered Telegram Markdown chunks, but there is no narrow adapter boundary for handing those chunks to a future Telegram transport.
constraints: Consume only WR-011 complete SemanticMessageChunk values; preserve each payload exactly and forward in source order.
Inject the transport as a local trait; do not implement network calls, credentials, secrets, SDKs, scheduler, receipt, retry, persistence, polling, or webhook behavior.
Do not render, split, parse, calculate, normalize, sort, or rewrite Weekly Radar content in this WI.

Complete Contract, spec/plan, TDD, focused/module-local/integration verification, strict AI Finish, archive, commit, publish, merge, close, and remote branch cleanup according to the recorded repository lifecycle.
intent.rationale: A small injected transport boundary lets later infrastructure choose the Telegram client while keeping rendering, semantic splitting, domain judgment, and publication lifecycle concerns in their existing or future Work Items.
